The problem with getting Steam running on Linux is that it's not JUST going it to run on Linux... It's getting it complied and running on Debian, Fedora, SUSE, ElementaryOS, Arch, etc.

Each distro has their own, independent file structure, so getting anything running "across the board" is extremely difficult.

Folders for icons move to different locations, depending on which distro you're talking about. Configuration files and daemon systems aren't the same across distros. Everything essentially changes across the board for one reason or another, which make compiling packages a pain in the ass.

As a Linux user, I was hoping Valve would "bring balance to the force" here, creating a need for a standard file structure, so that it's easier to compile packages for programs. But, instead, they appear to have taken the easy way out and just created their own distro (SteamOS) which they can control.
